# What needs approval in a Newton local historic district?

> In a Newton local historic district, exterior changes, including hardscaping, need review by the Historic District Commission. Visible alterations need a Certificate of Appropriateness. In-kind work, changes that can't be seen, and excluded work can get a Certificate of Non-Applicability, and in-kind repairs may qualify for administrative approval.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-local-historic-district-review/
- Topic: Historic
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Historic Preservation](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/historic-preservation); [Auburndale Historic District Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/local-historic-district-commissions/auburndale-hdc)

## What the City says

- Exterior changes in a local historic district, including hardscaping, require HDC review. (Source: [Historic Preservation](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/historic-preservation))
- A Certificate of Appropriateness covers visible alterations the commission finds appropriate. (Source: [Auburndale Historic District Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/local-historic-district-commissions/auburndale-hdc))
- A Certificate of Non-Applicability covers in-kind work, changes that can't be seen, or excluded work. (Source: [Auburndale Historic District Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/local-historic-district-commissions/auburndale-hdc))
- Exterior building changes require an application, and in-kind repairs may qualify for administrative approval. (Source: [Auburndale Historic District Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/local-historic-district-commissions/auburndale-hdc))

## Questions and answers

### Do I need approval to replace windows in a historic district?

Exterior building changes need an application. In-kind work may qualify for a Certificate of Non-Applicability or administrative approval. (Source: [Auburndale Historic District Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/local-historic-district-commissions/auburndale-hdc))

### Does a patio or walkway need review?

The City says exterior changes, including hardscaping, need HDC review. (Source: [Historic Preservation](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/historic-preservation))

### What is a Certificate of Appropriateness?

Approval for visible alterations that the commission finds appropriate. (Source: [Auburndale Historic District Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/local-historic-district-commissions/auburndale-hdc))

## What to confirm with the City

- Whether your property is inside a local historic district.
- Which certificate your project needs.
- Contact: [Historic Preservation](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/historic-preservation)

## Sources

- [Historic Preservation](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/historic-preservation) — checked Nov 13, 2026
- [Auburndale Historic District Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/local-historic-district-commissions/auburndale-hdc) — checked Nov 13, 2026

# When does an addition or remodel trigger Newton's demolition delay ordinance?

> Newton says an addition to a building over 50 years old may qualify as partial demolition if it removes 50% or more of the roof or removes or encloses 50% or more of an exterior wall. These projects must be submitted for historical review. The Commission may also review removal of historic architectural features in certain cases.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-partial-demolition-rules/
- Topic: Historic
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Newton Historical Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/newton-historical-commission); [https://www.newtonma.gov/how-do-i/view/frequently-asked-questions](https://www.newtonma.gov/how-do-i/view/frequently-asked-questions)

## Roof and exterior wall thresholds

- Newton identifies removal of 50% or more of a roof, or removal or enclosure of 50% or more of an exterior wall, as possible partial demolition. (Source: [Newton Historical Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/newton-historical-commission))

## Historic review

- Newton's historic review process covers partial demolition of buildings over 50 years old. (Source: [Newton Historic Preservation, Submit an Application](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/submit-an-application))

## Questions and answers

### Can adding a large rear addition trigger demolition review?

Yes. Newton says an addition may qualify as partial demolition when it involves removal of at least half of the roof or removal or enclosure of at least half of an exterior wall on a structure over 50 years old. (Source: [Newton Historical Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/newton-historical-commission))

## What to confirm with the City

- The structure's age and whether the 50-year threshold is met
- How Newton measures the roof or exterior-wall percentage
- Whether the work removes or alters character-defining historic features
- Whether the structure is in a Local Historic District, is a Landmark, or has a Preservation Restriction
- Whether the project also requires a building permit or zoning relief
- Contact: [Newton Historical Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/newton-historical-commission)

## Sources

- [Newton Historical Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/historic-preservation/newton-historical-commission) — checked Nov 13, 2026
- [https://www.newtonma.gov/how-do-i/view/frequently-asked-questions](https://www.newtonma.gov/how-do-i/view/frequently-asked-questions) — checked Nov 13, 2026

# Can you discharge a sump pump into the street or sewer in Newton, MA?

> The official sources reviewed do not establish a complete Newton homeowner rule for every sump-pump discharge location. Newton warns that stormwater and groundwater entering the sanitary sewer can overload the system. Confirm the allowed discharge route with Newton Utilities or Engineering before installing or changing a sump-pump connection.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-sump-pump-drainage-rules/
- Topic: Site & environment
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Newton Sanitary Sewer Overflow Alerts](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/public-works/utilities-division/sanitary-sewer-overflow-alerts); [Newton Engineering Division](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/public-works/engineering)

## Sanitary sewer capacity

- Newton identifies stormwater and groundwater entering the sanitary sewer system as a possible cause of sewer overload and sanitary sewer overflows. (Source: [Newton Sanitary Sewer Overflow Alerts](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/public-works/utilities-division/sanitary-sewer-overflow-alerts))

## Discharge approval

- Newton Engineering reviews drainage projects and site plans involving new drainage. (Source: [Newton Engineering Division](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/public-works/engineering))

## Questions and answers

### Does the cited Newton source establish that every street discharge is allowed or prohibited?

No. The source explains the sewer-overflow concern but does not establish a complete homeowner discharge rule. Confirm the proposed route with the City. (Source: [Newton Sanitary Sewer Overflow Alerts](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/public-works/utilities-division/sanitary-sewer-overflow-alerts))

## What to confirm with the City

- Whether discharge to the sanitary sewer is prohibited for the property
- Whether discharge to the storm drain or street is allowed
- Whether on-site infiltration is required or permitted
- Whether the proposed outlet affects neighboring property or public infrastructure
- Any required Engineering permit or drainage plan
- Contact: [Newton Public Works, Utilities Division](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/public-works)

# Do I need a permit to cut down a tree in Newton, MA?

> Often, yes. Trees 6 inches or more in diameter at breast height (measured 4½ feet above grade) on covered land are protected. You need a tree permit before removing a protected tree or starting work under an Exterior Work Permit. Even exempt trees need an exemption permit before removal.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-tree-preservation-ordinance/
- Topic: Site & environment
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000); [Tree Preservation Ordinance](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/parks-recreation-culture/urban-forestry/tree-preservation-ordinance)

## What the ordinance says

- Protected trees include trees at least 6 inches DBH on covered land, plus replacement trees (Sec. 21-81). (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000))
- DBH is measured 4½ feet above grade at the base of the tree (Sec. 21-81). (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000))
- A tree permit is required before removing a protected, non-exempt tree, or before starting work under an Exterior Work Permit (Sec. 21-82(b)). (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000))
- Even an exempt tree requires an exemption permit before removal (Sec. 21-82(c)). (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000))

## Replacement

- Required replacement is due within 18 months of the tree permit, or before the property changes hands, whichever comes first (Sec. 21-85(a)). (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000))
- Replacement trees must be planted on the same lot (Sec. 21-85(a)(2)). (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000))
- Applicants may plant replacements, pay in lieu, or combine the two. (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/parks-recreation-culture/urban-forestry/tree-preservation-ordinance))
- Replacement trees are protected and get at least Significant Tree status, whatever their trunk size (Sec. 21-85(a)(5)). (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000))

## Questions and answers

### What size tree is protected in Newton?

Trees at least 6 inches DBH on covered land, measured 4½ feet above grade. (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000))

### Do I need a tree permit for a construction project?

A tree permit is required before starting work under an Exterior Work Permit (Sec. 21-82(b)). (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000))

### Can I pay instead of replanting?

Yes. The City lists planting, payment in lieu, or a combination. (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/parks-recreation-culture/urban-forestry/tree-preservation-ordinance))

### When must replacement trees be planted?

Within 18 months of the tree permit, or before the property changes hands, whichever comes first. (Source: [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000))

## What to confirm with the City

- Whether your land is 'covered land' under the ordinance.
- Replacement amounts from the City's current table.
- Contact: [Tree Preservation Ordinance](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/parks-recreation-culture/urban-forestry/tree-preservation-ordinance)

## Sources

- [Tree Preservation Ordinance text (Ch. 21, Art. III)](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/117204/638445534507730000) — checked Nov 13, 2026
- [Tree Preservation Ordinance](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/parks-recreation-culture/urban-forestry/tree-preservation-ordinance) — checked Nov 13, 2026

# How do wetlands protection laws affect home projects in Newton, MA?

> Newton requires Conservation Commission review for land-altering work within 100 feet of a vegetated wetland, intermittent stream, or pond; within 200 feet of a perennial stream; or in a FEMA or City floodplain. The state Wetlands Protection Act also regulates alteration of protected resource areas. A permit may be required before work begins.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-wetlands-protection-by-law/
- Topic: Site & environment
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev); [Massachusetts General Laws, Chapter 131, Section 40, Wetlands Protection Act](https://malegislature.gov/Laws/GeneralLaws/PartI/TitleXIX/Chapter131/Section40)

## Newton review areas

- Newton identifies work within 100 feet of a vegetated wetland, intermittent stream, or pond and within 200 feet of a perennial stream as requiring Conservation Commission review. (Source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev))

## State Wetlands Protection Act

- Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 131, Section 40 regulates removal, filling, dredging, or alteration of specified wetlands and other protected resource areas. (Source: [Massachusetts General Laws, Chapter 131, Section 40, Wetlands Protection Act](https://malegislature.gov/Laws/GeneralLaws/PartI/TitleXIX/Chapter131/Section40))

## Questions and answers

### Does wetlands review apply only when a homeowner builds directly in a wetland?

No. Newton identifies review areas extending beyond the resource itself, including the 100-foot and 200-foot areas listed in its wetlands guidance. (Source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev))

## What to confirm with the City

- Whether the property contains or is near a regulated resource area
- The exact resource-area boundary and applicable review distance
- Whether the proposed work is exempt or requires an RDA or NOI
- Whether FEMA or City floodplain rules also apply
- Whether tree, stormwater, engineering, or building permits are separately required
- Contact: [Newton Conservation Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office)

## Sources

- [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev) — checked Nov 13, 2026

# Stormwater, wetlands and flood zones for home projects

Projects that add roof or paved area, move soil, or sit near water often need reviews beyond the building permit. The key facts are how much new impervious area you add, how much land you disturb, and whether the site is near mapped wetlands, streams or floodplain.

## Stormwater

Impervious surfaces such as roofs, driveways and patios send rainwater off the site instead of letting it soak in. Many communities require a stormwater permit above a size threshold, and some also require one for retaining walls or excavation dewatering. To answer the question, measure:

- New impervious area in square feet (additions, garages, driveways, patios).

- Total land disturbed during construction.

- Whether you need a new retaining wall because of a grade change, or will pump water out of trenches.

## Wetlands, streams and floodplains

Work in or near wetland resource areas and their buffer zones is regulated under state and local wetlands law, usually through the local conservation commission. Mapped floodplains can add construction requirements and review. A map layer showing nothing is useful, but a layer that fails to load tells you nothing. Confirm when in doubt.

## What HPP applies in Newton, Massachusetts

- Disturbing more than 5,000 sq ft of land requires a stormwater management and erosion control permit under Newton's ordinance, subject to its exceptions and waivers ([Engineering / Stormwater Management](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/public-works/engineering)).

- New impervious area of 401–1,000 sq ft is Newton's Minor Stormwater category. More than 1,000 sq ft calls for confirming the Major pathway.

- A new retaining wall needed because of a grade change, and trench dewatering, are also Minor Stormwater categories.

- If the property touches mapped wetlands, streams or floodplain, HPP routes exterior work to [Conservation review](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev). It reads the [Floodplains GIS Layer](https://gisweb.newtonma.gov/server/rest/services/Data/MapServer/41), [Wetlands GIS Layer](https://gisweb.newtonma.gov/server/rest/services/Data/MapServer/27) and [Streams GIS Layer](https://gisweb.newtonma.gov/server/rest/services/Data/MapServer/16).

- If the measurements are unknown, HPP lists stormwater as needs confirmation instead of assuming no permit applies.

## Sources

- [Engineering / Stormwater Management](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/public-works/engineering)
- [Wetlands Permitting](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev)
- [Floodplains GIS Layer](https://gisweb.newtonma.gov/server/rest/services/Data/MapServer/41)
- [Wetlands GIS Layer](https://gisweb.newtonma.gov/server/rest/services/Data/MapServer/27)
- [Streams GIS Layer](https://gisweb.newtonma.gov/server/rest/services/Data/MapServer/16)
Newton sources last verified September 19, 2026.

# What lead paint containment rules apply when renovating an older Newton home?

> Massachusetts requires lead-safe renovation work by a licensed lead-safe renovation contractor when paid work in a pre-1978 home disturbs more than 6 square feet of painted surface per room indoors or more than 20 square feet outdoors. A lead-safe renovation project is different from a deleading project. Confirm which rules apply before disturbing painted surfaces.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-lead-paint-renovation-rules/
- Topic: Site & environment
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Massachusetts Lead-Safe Renovation for Homeowners](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/lead-safe-renovation-for-homeowners)

## When the lead-safe renovation rule applies

- Massachusetts applies its lead-safe renovation requirements to paid work in pre-1978 housing when more than 6 square feet of painted surface per room is disturbed indoors or more than 20 square feet is disturbed outdoors. (Source: [Massachusetts Lead-Safe Renovation for Homeowners](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/lead-safe-renovation-for-homeowners))

## Renovation versus deleading

- Massachusetts distinguishes renovation work from work intended to abate lead hazards or obtain a Letter of Compliance. (Source: [Massachusetts Lead-Safe Renovation for Homeowners](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/lead-safe-renovation-for-homeowners))

## Questions and answers

### Does every repair in a pre-1978 home require a deleading project?

No. Massachusetts distinguishes lead-safe renovation work from deleading. The applicable requirement depends on the work's purpose and the amount of painted surface disturbed. (Source: [Massachusetts Lead-Safe Renovation for Homeowners](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/lead-safe-renovation-for-homeowners))

## What to confirm with the City

- The home's construction year
- Whether painted surfaces contain lead or require testing
- The interior or exterior area of painted surface to be disturbed
- Whether the project is renovation work or deleading
- Whether a licensed lead-safe renovation supervisor must be on site
- Whether historic-property restrictions affect component removal or replacement
- Contact: [Massachusetts Lead-Safe Renovation for Homeowners](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/lead-safe-renovation-for-homeowners)

## Sources

- [Massachusetts Lead-Safe Renovation for Homeowners](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/lead-safe-renovation-for-homeowners) — checked Nov 13, 2026

# What rules apply to building or renovating a home in a FEMA flood zone in Newton, MA?

> Newton identifies FEMA floodplain and City floodplain areas as locations where land-altering work must be reviewed by the Conservation Commission. The exact building elevation, flood-resistant construction, and substantial-improvement requirements depend on the property's mapped flood zone and proposed work. Do not rely on a general 50% rule without confirming the applicable code and floodplain provisions.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-floodplain-construction-rules/
- Topic: Site & environment
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev); [Massachusetts State Building Code, 780 CMR](https://www.mass.gov/massachusetts-state-building-code-780-cmr)

## Newton floodplain review

- Newton's wetlands guidance identifies FEMA Floodplain and City Floodplain as areas where land-altering work must be reviewed and permitted by the Conservation Commission. (Source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev))

## Building-code requirements

- The Massachusetts State Building Code includes flood-protection provisions, and the applicable requirements depend on the type and location of the building. (Source: [Massachusetts State Building Code, 780 CMR](https://www.mass.gov/massachusetts-state-building-code-780-cmr))

## Questions and answers

### Does the 50% substantial-improvement threshold answer every Newton floodplain question?

No. The sources reviewed do not establish that one threshold resolves every case. Confirm the mapped flood zone, current code provision, and City floodplain ordinance for the specific property. (Source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev); [Massachusetts State Building Code, 780 CMR](https://www.mass.gov/massachusetts-state-building-code-780-cmr))

## What to confirm with the City

- The property's FEMA flood zone and base flood elevation
- Whether the parcel is also within a City floodplain
- Applicable substantial-improvement and substantial-damage definitions
- Required lowest-floor and equipment elevations
- Flood-resistant construction requirements
- Whether a Conservation Commission filing or engineering plan is needed
- Contact: [Newton Conservation Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office)

# What work is restricted within the 100-foot wetland buffer zone in Newton, MA?

> Newton requires Conservation Commission review for land-altering work within 100 feet of a vegetated wetland, intermittent stream, or pond. The City also identifies a 200-foot review area near perennial streams. The exact restrictions depend on the resource area, proposed activity, and applicable exemptions.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-buffer-zone-rules/
- Topic: Site & environment
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev)

## The 100-foot area

- Newton identifies the 100-foot area near vegetated wetlands, intermittent streams, and ponds as an area where land-altering work must be reviewed and permitted by the Conservation Commission. (Source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev))

## Activities that may be regulated

- Newton lists grading, construction, tree or shrub removal, and drainage projects among land-altering activities subject to review. (Source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev))

## Questions and answers

### Can I grade or install drainage within the 100-foot area without checking?

No. Newton expressly lists grading and drainage projects among activities that may require Conservation Commission review. (Source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev))

## What to confirm with the City

- Whether the property is within the 100-foot or 200-foot review area
- The exact resource-area boundary and whether a survey is needed
- Whether the work is exempt or requires an RDA or NOI
- Whether a City floodplain or stormwater review is also required
- Whether tree-removal or construction permits are required separately
- Contact: [Newton Conservation Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office)

# When do you need to file an RDA or NOI with the Newton Conservation Commission?

> Newton uses a Request for Determination of Applicability (RDA) and a Notice of Intent (NOI) as separate wetlands filing paths. The City lists a $50 filing fee for each application type. An NOI requires additional materials, including scaled plans, a project narrative, performance-standard information, and abutter-notification documents.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-conservation-commission-filing/
- Topic: Site & environment
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev)

## RDA application

- Newton lists an RDA Process Instructions and Checklist, WPA Form 1, scaled plans, and a $50 City filing fee as RDA application materials. (Source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev))

## NOI application

- Newton lists WPA Form 3, scaled plans, a project narrative, performance-standard information, a $50 filing fee, and abutter-notification documents among NOI application materials. (Source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev))

## Questions and answers

### Does an RDA require the same submission package as an NOI?

No. Newton lists different filing materials for the two application types. The City should confirm which filing applies to the proposed activity. (Source: [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev))

## What to confirm with the City

- Whether the project requires an RDA, NOI, or another determination
- Whether the activity is within a regulated resource area
- The applicable filing fee at the time of submission
- The plans, narrative, and technical attachments needed
- The current abutter list and proof-of-service requirements
- Whether separate building, Engineering, tree, or historic permits are required
- Contact: [Newton Conservation Commission](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office)

## Sources

- [Newton Wetlands Permitting Information](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/planning/divisions/conservation-office/wetlands-permitting-rev) — checked Nov 13, 2026

# When does a residential project trigger a Newton Stormwater Management Permit?

> Newton's stormwater ordinance requires a permit before certain land-disturbance projects that could disturb more than 5,000 square feet. It also identifies residential projects creating 401 to 1,000 square feet of new impervious area as a minor stormwater-review category. Other triggers include certain retaining walls and trench excavation requiring dewatering.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-stormwater-management-permit/
- Topic: Site & environment
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Newton Stormwater Management and Erosion Control Ordinance](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/104834/638260676720970000)

## Land disturbance threshold

- Newton's ordinance lists projects that will or could disturb more than 5,000 square feet of land as requiring a stormwater management and erosion control permit. (Source: [Newton Stormwater Management and Erosion Control Ordinance](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/104834/638260676720970000))

## New impervious area

- The ordinance lists residential development or redevelopment creating 401 to 1,000 square feet of new impervious area as a minor stormwater management category. (Source: [Newton Stormwater Management and Erosion Control Ordinance](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/104834/638260676720970000))

## Questions and answers

### Can a small residential project trigger stormwater review even when it disturbs less than 5,000 square feet?

Yes. The ordinance separately lists certain residential projects creating 401 to 1,000 square feet of new impervious area as a minor stormwater category. (Source: [Newton Stormwater Management and Erosion Control Ordinance](https://www.newtonma.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/104834/638260676720970000))

## What to confirm with the City

- The total land-disturbance area
- The net new impervious area
- Whether the project is a residential development with four or fewer units
- Whether a retaining wall or dewatering trench triggers review
- Whether an exemption under Newton's stormwater rules applies
- Required calculations, plans, and professional certifications
- Contact: [Newton Engineering Division](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/public-works/engineering)

## Sources

# When is an on-site drywell or stormwater infiltration system required in Newton, MA?

> Newton's stormwater ordinance regulates certain land-disturbance and new-impervious-area projects, but the sources reviewed do not establish one universal drywell size or a citywide rule requiring every homeowner to install a drywell. Whether an infiltration system is needed depends on the project, site conditions, and Newton's stormwater requirements.

# Do new homes and renovations in Newton have to be all-electric?

> Yes, for projects that trigger the rules. Newton says complete building permit applications received after January 1, 2024 fall under the Specialized Energy Code. Starting January 1, 2025, all new construction and major renovation projects must electrify heating, cooling, cooking and clothes drying.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/newton-energy-code-all-electric-rules/
- Topic: Energy & mechanical
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Energy Code / Fossil Fuel-Free](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/energy-code)

## What Newton says

- Complete building permit applications received after January 1, 2024 are subject to the Specialized Code. (Source: [Energy Code / Fossil Fuel-Free](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/energy-code))
- Since January 1, 2025, all new construction and major renovation projects must electrify heating, cooling, cooking and clothes drying, with electricity or thermal solar for hot water. (Source: [Energy Code / Fossil Fuel-Free](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/energy-code))
- Newton's 2026 notice says projects that trigger the fossil-fuel ordinance must be fully all-electric. (Source: [Energy Code / Fossil Fuel-Free](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/energy-code))
- Electrical permit applications are filed online. (Source: [Electrical Permits](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/electrical-permits))

## Questions and answers

### Does Newton require all-electric homes?

For new construction and major renovations, Newton requires electrified heating, cooling, cooking and clothes drying (since January 1, 2025). (Source: [Energy Code / Fossil Fuel-Free](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/energy-code))

### What energy code applies in Newton?

The Specialized Code applies to complete building permit applications received after January 1, 2024. (Source: [Energy Code / Fossil Fuel-Free](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/energy-code))

### Do I need a permit to install a heat pump?

Heat pumps involve electrical work, and Newton electrical permits are filed online by a licensed electrician. Confirm any other permits with the City. (Source: [Electrical Permits](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/electrical-permits))

## What to confirm with the City

- Whether your renovation counts as a 'major renovation' under the ordinance.
- Which permits a heat pump installation needs.
- Contact: [Inspectional Services — Contact Us](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/contact-us)

# Can a homeowner do electrical, plumbing or gas work in Newton, MA?

> Newton's electrical and plumbing/gas permit submissions require an appropriately signed license. Massachusetts issues plumbing permits only to licensed plumbers. The state lists minor repairs, such as fixing a leaky faucet or clearing a blocked drain, as not needing a permit.

- Canonical page: https://home-project-planner-mvp.vercel.app/guides/electrical-plumbing-gas-permits-newton-homeowners/
- Topic: Contractors & trades
- Updated: November 13, 2026
- Publisher: Home Project Planner (independent; not affiliated with the City of Newton)

Official source: [Electrical Permits](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/electrical-permits); [Plumbing & Gas Permits](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/plumbing-gas-permits); [Plumbers and Gas Fitters Consumer Fact Sheet (Mass.gov)](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/plumbers-and-gas-fitters-consumer-fact-sheet)

## Newton requirements

- Electrical permit submissions require an appropriately signed electrical license. (Source: [Electrical Permits](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/electrical-permits))
- Electrical submissions need liability insurance and workers' compensation unless the applicant is a sole proprietor. (Source: [Electrical Permits](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/electrical-permits))
- Plumbing and gas submissions require an appropriately signed plumbing or gas license. (Source: [Plumbing & Gas Permits](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/plumbing-gas-permits))
- Replacing a gas water heater requires both a plumbing permit and a gas permit. (Source: [Plumbing & Gas Permits](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/plumbing-gas-permits))

## Massachusetts rules

- Massachusetts issues plumbing permits only to licensed plumbers. (Source: [Plumbers and Gas Fitters Consumer Fact Sheet (Mass.gov)](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/plumbers-and-gas-fitters-consumer-fact-sheet))
- Only licensed professionals may install, remove or repair plumbing. (Source: [Plumbers and Gas Fitters Consumer Fact Sheet (Mass.gov)](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/plumbers-and-gas-fitters-consumer-fact-sheet))
- Fixing a leaky faucet, valve or other working part, or clearing a blocked drain, is a minor repair that does not need a permit. (Source: [Plumbers and Gas Fitters Consumer Fact Sheet (Mass.gov)](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/plumbers-and-gas-fitters-consumer-fact-sheet))
- Licensed master or journeyman plumbers may do gas fitting, but a gas-fitter license does not cover plumbing work. (Source: [Plumbers and Gas Fitters Consumer Fact Sheet (Mass.gov)](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/plumbers-and-gas-fitters-consumer-fact-sheet))

## Questions and answers

### Can I pull my own plumbing permit in Massachusetts?

The state says plumbing permits are issued only to licensed plumbers. (Source: [Plumbers and Gas Fitters Consumer Fact Sheet (Mass.gov)](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/plumbers-and-gas-fitters-consumer-fact-sheet))

### Do I need a permit to fix a leaky faucet?

No. The state lists fixing a leaky faucet, valve or other working part, or clearing a blocked drain, as minor repairs that need no permit. (Source: [Plumbers and Gas Fitters Consumer Fact Sheet (Mass.gov)](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/plumbers-and-gas-fitters-consumer-fact-sheet))

### What permits does a gas water heater replacement need in Newton?

Both a plumbing permit and a gas permit. (Source: [Plumbing & Gas Permits](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/plumbing-gas-permits))

### What does a Newton electrical permit application need?

An appropriately signed electrical license, plus liability insurance and workers' compensation unless the applicant is a sole proprietor. (Source: [Electrical Permits](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/electrical-permits))

### Can a gas fitter do plumbing?

No. The state says a gas-fitter license does not authorize plumbing work. (Source: [Plumbers and Gas Fitters Consumer Fact Sheet (Mass.gov)](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/plumbers-and-gas-fitters-consumer-fact-sheet))

## What to confirm with the City

- Whether any homeowner electrical permit option applies to your work. HPP did not find this on the City pages it reviewed.
- Contact: [Inspectional Services — Contact Us](https://www.newtonma.gov/government/inspectional-services/contact-us)
